author: Caroline Bowyer
title: 'No way': Mooresville mayor will not resign amid 3 lawsuits, alleged pants-less town hall incident - NewsBreak
text:
By Caroline Bowyer ,
2 hours ago
MOORESVILLE, N.C. (QUEEN CITY NEWS) — Mooresville’s mayor is not going anywhere, despite town commissioners urging him to resign.
Chris Carney is in the spotlight over an alleged pants-less incident caught on surveillance video inside Town Hall in 2024. It’s led to lawsuits against the town.
Carney said despite the drama earlier this week, it’s been business as usual ever since. He has about 19 months left in his term and he’s planning to keep serving. But another commissioner said this may not be the end of the board’s efforts to push for his resignation.
“You’ve got to remember, this was in 2024,” said Carney. “It’s been so long ago and obviously, as I tell people, I was fighting through a lot of stuff at the time.”
Driver reported leak 20 minutes before deadly Mooresville tanker explosion: NTSB A year and a half later though, those actions are prompting some Mooresville commissioners to take action against Carney.
“There are things, further actions that the board can take to continue to communicate to him that we stand behind the resolution, but I don’t feel like it’s appropriate to comment on what those actions are at this time,” said Commissioner Dana Tucker.
Tucker put together a presentation about the ways he believes Carney went against the board’s code of ethics. It’s what prompted Monday’s vote of no confidence urging Carney to leave his position, and what could prompt further action against him.
“At the end of the day, each person is just trying to survive on their own political merit,” said Carney. “I know this has been a lot, and although we keep saying let’s let the truth come out in the lawsuits, they’ve had to answer some questions. I’m sure they’re tired of it.”
The lawsuits he’s referencing are against the town. Three former employees filed them claiming retaliation.
“One thing our board did that people don’t realize is they asked me to step out, and they hired a complete independent group to look into it,” said Carney. “We have a whole report that says it just never happened. The sad part is I think these people are going to realize they did this to themselves. Because through that investigation they found out about the next person. And then through that investigation they found out about the next person.”
Mooresville Town Hall. The people behind those lawsuits claim they were fired after raising concerns about an incident involving Carney inside Town Hall in October 2024.
“I’ve made all the statements about that I want to make,” said Carney. “I am sorry for the distraction, but as any commissioner who wants to be honest with you, I owned it the next day.”
Carney blamed alcohol for his poor decision-making that night, less than a year into his first term, where he was allegedly caught on internal surveillance video without pants on and with a female town communications consultant.
“I’m in a so much better place and I’m really thankful actually,” he said. “It was a great turning point for me.”
Carney’s confident this one night won’t overshadow what he and his wife have done for the town the past several years.
“I’m pretty proud of when I finally retire, the legacy we’ve left in this town and I hope people will appreciate we did it because we love not only this town but the citizens and we’ve been thankful to live here,” he said.
Carney told Queen City News he does not plan to run for re-election for mayor or any other office. He said that’s always been the case, and this situation does not influence that decision whatsoever.
